newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco seeks partnership to tackle pollution.
newsitem.headline: Morocco seeks partnership to tackle pollution.

text.p: A Moroccan minister who said recently that damage to the environment cost the country $2.3 billion a year called on Monday for a partnership with industry to overcome the problem.
Environment Minister Nouredine Ben Omar Alami told a seminar that Morocco and Germany were to set up a fund to battle pollution and this would be used to help industry.
He said the national environment council was surveying environmental damage and pollution with the aim of drawing up a strategy in partnership with businesses to combat this.
A statement read on behalf of Public Works Minister Abdelaziz Meziane said Morocco had made great progress since an environment ministry was created last year but still had much to do.

"I would pinpoint in particular the waste produced by towns and main industries which to this day are dumped without treatment...rivers and reservoirs asphyxiated by pollution, the seaside which suffers permanent damage to the waters and sand."
The two-day meeting is aimed at drawing up an action plan to combat environmental damage and look at possible new laws.
